facts: A prisoner condemned to death over eight years ago claims that it is not lawful to hang him now.
He was the principal accused in the case and, so to say, the archvillian of a villainous piece.
The plan was ingeniously fiendish and the appellant was the architect.
There is no question that the learned Sessions Judge very rightly sentenced him to death but that was in January 1975.
Since then he has been kept in solitary confinement, quite contrary to our ruling in Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration 1979 Indlaw SC 329.
Before that he was a 'prisoner under remand' for two years.
issues: Whether it is lawful to hang the prisoner after keeping him in jail for ten years, eight of which in illegal solitary confinement?
petitioner_arguments: The prisoner claims that to take away his life after keeping him in jail for ten years, eight of which in illegal solitary confinement, is a gross violation of the Fundamental Right guaranteed by Art. 21 of the Constitution.
He argues that prolonged delay in executing a sentence of death can make the punishment when it comes inhuman and degrading.
respondent_arguments: The respondent/defending party does not provide any specific arguments in this judgment.
court_reasoning: The court notes that while the murders were wicked and diabolic, justice to the killer too and not justice untempered by mercy that we dispense.

The court observes that prolonged delay when it arises from factors outside the control of the condemned man can render a decision to carry out the sentence of death an inhuman and degrading punishment.
The court holds that the cause of the delay is immaterial when the sentence is death.
holding: The court allows the appeal and commutes the sentence of death to imprisonment for life.
